title: Can you reach the last index?
summary: Each stone says how far you can leap from it; track the farthest stone reachable to know whether you can cross.
goal: Decide whether the far bank can be reached

mapping.story: How far you can leap from a stone

examples.label: Can cross
examples.explanation: Leap 1 stone, then 3, to reach the end.

examples.label: Stuck at a zero
examples.explanation: Every route lands on the 0 at position 3 and cannot go further.

examples.label: Already there
examples.explanation: The first stone is the last.

ladder.name: Try every route
ladder.idea: From each stone, recursively try every possible leap and see if any route reaches the end.

ladder.name: Mark reachable stones
ladder.idea: Walk the stones in order; from every reachable stone, mark all stones it can leap to.
ladder.insight: Many routes reach the same stone, and what happens next depends only on the stone, not the route. Marking each stone once removes the repetition.

ladder.name: Track the farthest reach
ladder.idea: Walk the stones keeping the farthest stone reachable so far. If you ever stand beyond it, you are stuck.
ladder.insight: The reachable stones always form one unbroken stretch from the start, so a single number, its far end, describes all of them.

transfer.problem: A delivery van can drive a certain distance from each fuel station. Can it get from the first station to the last?
transfer.explanation: Each station extends the farthest point reachable; if you ever arrive beyond that point, the trip fails.

selfCheck: Stops with False the moment a position is beyond the reach.
Updates the reach with i + nums[i].
Returns True for a single stone.
